newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells ruling People's Alliance working committee that defence and government spending will be reduced from next year as lot of money spent on war and arms this year. Funds released from reduction of flour subsidy can be spent for development.
Joint plantations labour unions meeting in Badulla resolve to take trade union action in November to get wage hike and cost of living allowance.
Shipping Minister M.H.M. Ashraff says Moslem Congress to talk to Tamil parties next week on solution to ethnic problem.
Telia A.B. Sweden to invest five billion rupees to set up wireless local loop telephone network in island in next two years.
Several low-lying areas submerged by floods after heavy rains. Traffic from Avissawella to hill country disrupted by floods.
Police find vehicle used for killing of opposition United National Party supporters in Negombo.
Gunmen shoot dead opposition United National Party pradeshiya sabha (local council) member in Negombo.
Canadian investors ready to form joint ventures in Sri Lanka, International Development Council tells Deputy Finance Minister G.L. Peiris.
